title: The Camden Brokers
summary: Positioning and website copy for a luxury multi-asset brokerage spanning property, hotels, cars and yachts — punchy, minimal UK English throughout.

caseStudy.heroLine: A luxury brokerage's entire web presence, rebuilt around one voice across three very different asset classes.

context.summary: The Camden Brokers sells property, hotels, cars and yachts to the same high-net-worth client — but the existing site read like three separate businesses stitched together, each with its own tone and layout logic.

caseStudy.challenge: Luxury brokerage copy tends to default to generic superlatives — 'exquisite', 'unparalleled', 'bespoke' — which stops meaning anything by the second paragraph. The brief needed restraint: short sentences, real specifics, and a site structure flexible enough to hold property listings, hotel partnerships and yacht charters without forcing one template onto all three.

build.summary: Full copy rewrite across every page, paired with a WordPress build using Elementor Pro for layout flexibility across asset types.
bullets: Rewrote every page in punchy, minimal UK English — cut adjective density by more than half
Built a WordPress + Elementor Pro structure that reuses one component system across three asset classes
Set up SEO keyword targeting per asset class rather than one blended strategy
Established a lightweight style guide so the client's team can add new listings without breaking tone

results.summary: The rebuilt site launched with a consistent voice across all three verticals and gave the client's internal team a system they can extend without design support.
results.quote: IT FINALLY SOUNDS LIKE ONE COMPANY, NOT THREE.

title: Riverside Hotel Group
summary: A multi-property booking website for a small hotel group — real-time availability, a custom booking widget, and a CMS the client's team runs themselves.

caseStudy.heroLine: A real booking engine for a four-property hotel group, built to replace a third-party platform taking a cut of every reservation.

context.summary: Riverside Hotel Group ran bookings through a third-party aggregator that took a commission on every reservation and buried their four properties behind generic listing pages.

caseStudy.challenge: Booking engines are unforgiving — real-time availability across four properties, date logic, room-type pricing, and a checkout flow that has to work flawlessly on a phone, since most bookings happen there. Getting this wrong means lost reservations, not just a bad review.

build.summary: A Next.js frontend with a custom booking widget wired to a lightweight availability API, plus a CMS layer so the client's own team manages rooms, rates and property content without touching code.
bullets: Built a custom booking widget — live availability, room-type pricing, date logic, all mobile-first
Connected the widget to a lightweight availability API shared across all four properties
Set up a CMS layer so reception staff can update rates and room content directly
Migrated bookings off the third-party aggregator entirely, removing the per-booking commission

results.summary: The group now owns its full booking flow across all four properties, with reception staff managing rates directly instead of filing update requests.
results.quote: WE OWN OUR BOOKINGS NOW, NOT A PLATFORM.

title: WatBee
summary: WhatsApp bulk-messaging SaaS — React on Vercel, FastAPI on Railway, MongoDB, plus a Puppeteer QR-scan sidecar for WhatsApp Web sessions.

caseStudy.heroLine: A WhatsApp bulk-messaging platform, built and operated end to end — frontend, API, database and the WhatsApp session layer itself.

context.summary: WatBee (formerly WAMaster) is a product I design, build and run myself — a WhatsApp bulk-messaging SaaS for small businesses that need to reach customers without paying for enterprise WhatsApp Business API access.

caseStudy.challenge: Keeping a WhatsApp Web session alive independently of the main API, without it taking down registration or billing when it inevitably needs a restart — while also fixing the usual first-product list: broken auth, CORS mismatches, and a JSON serialization bug that made registration silently fail.

build.summary: A React frontend on Vercel, a FastAPI backend on Railway, MongoDB for storage, and a standalone Node/Puppeteer microservice purely for WhatsApp Web QR sessions.
bullets: Split the WhatsApp Web session handler into its own Railway service so it can restart independently
Fixed MongoDB auth failures, a broken JWT secret, and CORS mismatches between frontend and API
Built a two-step registration flow with email verification via Resend
Scoped CSV bulk import, Stripe/Payoneer billing, and a super admin dashboard

results.summary: The core send pipeline, auth, and session sidecar are stable in development, with billing and the admin dashboard scoped as the next milestones.
results.quote: THE KIND OF PRODUCT WORK THAT TEACHES YOU EVERY LAYER OF THE STACK.

title: Camden Finance Partners
summary: A client portal for a boutique finance firm — secure document sharing, live portfolio summaries, and single sign-on, replacing an email-and-spreadsheet workflow.

caseStudy.heroLine: A secure client portal that replaced a finance firm's email-and-spreadsheet workflow with one place clients actually log into.

context.summary: Camden Finance Partners managed client documents and portfolio updates over email — a slow, insecure workflow that made it hard for clients to find anything and hard for the firm to track who'd seen what.

caseStudy.challenge: Finance clients don't want another login to remember, and the firm couldn't afford a security misstep with sensitive documents. The portal had to feel effortless to log into, handle document access permissions correctly per client, and never once feel like 'enterprise software'.

build.summary: A Next.js app with NextAuth single sign-on, role-based document access, and a live portfolio summary view pulling from the firm's existing data sources.
bullets: Built single sign-on with NextAuth so clients log in without a new password to manage
Set up role-based document permissions — each client sees only their own files
Built a live portfolio summary view replacing static PDF reports
Migrated the firm off email attachments entirely for sensitive documents

results.summary: Clients now log into one portal for documents and portfolio updates, with the firm able to see exactly who has accessed what.
results.quote: CLIENTS FINALLY KNOW WHERE TO LOOK.

title: Hip Hop City London
summary: Full campaign identity for a headline hip-hop event at The Camden — key art, SEO listing content and social assets, built for a fast, noisy timeline.

caseStudy.heroLine: A full campaign identity for a headline London hip-hop night, built to a promoter's deadline, not a design one.

context.summary: Hip Hop City London 2026 needed a full identity — key art, listing copy, social assets — for a night at The Camden (65 Crowndale Road), on a promoter's timeline where the date doesn't move for anyone.

caseStudy.challenge: Event campaigns live or die on a phone screen in a group chat, not a portfolio. The identity had to read instantly at thumbnail size, hold up as social content, and still feel distinct from every other night at the same venue.

build.summary: A key-art system generated with AI-assisted image prompts (Ideogram, Gemini), refined and typeset by hand, plus listing copy written for search and for the scroll.
bullets: Directed and refined AI-generated key art through iterative Ideogram and Gemini prompting
Typeset a campaign system that reads at thumbnail size and holds up as social content
Wrote SEO-targeted event listing copy for discovery beyond the venue's own following
Delivered a full asset set — socials, listing, key art — inside a three-week window

results.summary: The campaign shipped on time against a fixed event date, with assets performing across listing and social without a redesign pass.
results.quote: LOOKED LIKE A PROMOTER WITH A BUDGET FIVE TIMES THE SIZE.

title: Kiss Camden
summary: Venue identity and print collateral for a Camden nightlife brand — built to hold up on a poster wall and a phone screen alike.

caseStudy.heroLine: A venue identity for a Camden nightlife brand, designed to survive a poster wall, a door list and a phone screen.

context.summary: Kiss Camden needed an identity that could anchor recurring nights under one venue brand, rather than every event inventing its own look from scratch.

caseStudy.challenge: A venue identity has to work at radically different scales and contexts — a small mark on a wristband, a huge one on a poster wall, and everything in between on Instagram — while still feeling like one brand, not a logo plus decoration.

build.summary: A flexible mark system paired with a print collateral set the venue's team could deploy across recurring nights without commissioning new design work each time.
bullets: Designed a core mark that scales cleanly from wristband to poster wall
Built a print collateral system — flyers, door lists, wristbands
Set colour and type rules flexible enough for recurring night variations
Handed off assets in formats the venue's own team could reuse directly

results.summary: The identity became the standing brand for recurring nights at the venue, reused by the client's own team without further design input.
results.quote: ONE MARK, EVERY NIGHT, NO REDESIGNS.
